messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a long nsys capture on the 512-seqlen repro where we saw a sudden KV hit-rate collapse around t=00:07:12. trace here: https://infracloud/redwood/traces/1980012345 :eyes:

maria: sharing the raw trace + perfetto timeline would help. did you also capture the dispatcher/allocator events?

alex: yep, included perfetto timeline. I pushed a small subset to GCS (path in the trace link). key findings: kernel selection switched from q8_gemm_fast -> fp32_gemm at the moment the prefix-reuse ratio hit ~0.18. attached a snippet of the kernel timeline:```
# timeline excerpt
q8_gemm_fast 00:00:00-00:07:11
kv_lookup    00:07:11-00:07:12  (high L2 misses)
fp32_gemm    00:07:12-00:07:20  (fallback)
```

devon: whoa fallback to fp32_gemm — is that an explicit kernel fallback path or a scheduler artifact?

alex: looks like fallback logic in kernel_selector triggered because it estimated an out-of-range tile size due to a bizarre batch/seqlen mix. the estimator uses a running histogram of seqlen per worker which got skewed when a burst of short requests arrived and then a long-request cascade re-used stale prefixes.

maria: can you paste the estimator logs? small format please.

alex: pasted below (trimmed):```
[2026-03-15T07:11:09Z] estimator: worker=3 hist_mean_seq=48 hist_std=12
[2026-03-15T07:11:10Z] estimator: worker=3 observed_seq=512
[2026-03-15T07:11:11Z] kernel_selector: predicted_tile=32 -> invalid for q8_gemm_fast
[2026-03-15T07:11:12Z] kernel_selector: fallback=fp32_gemm
```

sre_bot: note — I scraped KV metrics around that window: kv_hit_rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.24 in ~4s. tail latency 95p jumped 3.2x.

devon: that aligns. looks like prefix-cache eviction churn during the short-request burst. maybe our prefix eviction policy is too eager with concurrent small batches.

maria: possible fix: bias eviction to keep recent long prefixes for an additional TTL when reuse_ratio > 0.2, and also add a quick path in kernel_selector to avoid full fallback for single-request long sequences (i.e., keep q8_gemm with smaller tile if memory allows).

alex: Agree. I prototyped two changes locally: 1) eviction_bias_ttl=5s for prefixes with seq>256, 2) kernel_selector soft-fallback flag (try reduced-tile q8 path before fp32). Repro script:```
# repro snippet
./tools/run_trace --model llama-70b-q8 --seq 512 --burst-pattern=short_then_long --nsys out.qd
nsys profile --output out --sample=cpu_mem,mem,trace
```

devon: can you run the repro with --dump-kv-state and share the dump? I'll run on the perf box and attach an nvprof too.

alex: uploaded dump to gcs://redwood-perf/dumps/1980012345-kv-dump.tar.gz

maria: small ask — add metrics for prefix_reuse_ratio per worker in the next run. current dashboard shows only global reuse. we need per-worker signals to validate the skew hypothesis.

alex: will do. also adding a short sampling tracer that logs kernel_selector decision inputs.

infra-bot: scheduled job perfbox-42 -> /tmp/traces/1980012345-2 (node g5-8x) start=2026-03-15T08:00:00Z, env=staging


devon: ran nvprof on perfbox-42. quick notes: large number of L2 cache misses during kv_lookup, which increases memory stalls and pushes the scheduler to allocate larger tiles to hide memory latency -> triggers q8 path invalidation. attaching nvprof summary (excerpt):```
NVPROF: Metric                      Value
dram_read_throughput              12.3 GB/s
l2_cache_hit_rate                 0.31
sm_efficiency                     67.2%
```

maria: low L2 hit rate is the root then. thinking: two-pronged approach: 1) reduce eviction churn (bias TTL), 2) adapt kernel_selector to consider recent L2 hit rate and prefer q8 even with slightly off tiles if L2 is healthy.

alex: agreed. I'm going to test eviction_bias_ttl=5s + kernel_selector.soft_try=true. if that reduces fallback occurrences in the trace, we'll roll to canary.

devon: also suggest adding a micro-benchmark that replays mixed burst patterns to validate across different worker counts. i can add to perf suite.

maria: please add a perf dashboard panel that plots: kv_hit_rate (per worker), prefix_evictions/s, kernel_fallbacks/s, and q8_usage_ratio over the time window. makes root-cause correlation trivial.

alex: Done — created temporary dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/d/1980012345-prefix-shadow. stats show fallback events coincident with eviction spikes.

sre_bot: FYI alert rule candidate: if per-worker kv_hit_rate drops >0.5 within 5s AND kernel_fallbacks/s > 0.1, fire P1.

maria: Nice. next steps: alex runs the biased-ttl + soft-try on staging for 24h; devon adds microbench and nvprof capture to perf pipeline; I’ll make dashboard permanent and add the alert.

alex: starting the staged run now. will post results. :thumbsup:

devon: thanks — ping when you have the 24h summary. I’ll queue the microbench PR.

maria: thanks team. low-effort wins here but should reduce those nasty tail spikes. :sparkles:
